blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 1

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

Pearls

A Long known as the “Queen of Gems”, pearls possess a history and allure far beyond what today's wearer may recognize. Throughout much of recorded history, a natural pearl necklace comprised of matched spheres was a treasure of almost incomparable value, in fact, the most expensive jewelry in the world. Before the creation of cultured pearls in the early 1900s, natural pearls were so rare and expensive that they were reserved almost exclusively for the noble and very rich. The ancient Egyptians were particularly fond of their pearls. Many Egyptian leaders treasured pearls so much that they were often buried along with their cherished pearl collection. In the Orient and Persian Empire, pearls were ground into costly powders to cure anything from heart disease to epilepsy, with possible aphrodisiac uses as well. China's long recorded history also provides ample evidence of the importance of pearls.

B Pearls usually fall into three categories—natural pearls, cultured pearls and simulated pearls. A natural pearl forms when an irritant, such as a piece of sand, works its way into a particular species of oyster, mussel, or clam. As a defense mechanism, the mollusk secretes a fluid to coat the irritant. Layer upon layer of this coating is deposited on the irritant until a lustrous pearl is formed. A cultured pearl undergoes the same process. The only difference between natural pearls and cultured pearls is that the irritant is a surgically implanted bead or piece of shell called Mother of Pearl. Often, these shells are ground oyster shells that are worth significant amounts of money in their own right as irritant-catalysts for quality pearls. The resulting core is much larger than in a natural pearl. Imitation pearls are a different story altogether. In most cases, a glass bead is dipped into a solution made from fish scales. This coating is thin and may eventually wear off. One can usually tell an imitation by biting on it. The island of Mallorca in Spain is known for its imitation pearl industry.

C Regardless of the method used to acquire a pearl, the process usually takes several years. Mussels must reach a mature age, which can take up to 3 years, and then be implanted or naturally receive an irritant. Once the irritant is in place, it can take up to another 3 years for the pearl to reach its full size. Often, the irritant may be rejected, the pearl will be terrifically misshapen, or the oyster may simply die from disease or countless other complications. By the end of a 5 to 10 year cycle, only 50% of the oysters will have survived. And of the pearls produced, only approximately 5% are of a quality substantial enough for top jewelry makers.

D How can untrained eyes determine a pearl's worth? Luster and size are generally considered the two main factors to look for. Luster, for instance, depends on the fineness and evenness of the layers. The deeper the glow, the more perfect the shape and surface, the more valuable they are. Size, on the other hand, has to do with the age of the oyster that created the pearl (the more mature oysters produce larger pearls) and the location in which the pearl was cultured. The South Sea waters of Australia tend to produce the larger pearls; probably because the water along the coastline is supplied with rich nutrients from the ocean floor. Also, the type of mussel being common to the area seems to possess a predilection for producing comparatively large pearls.

E In general, cultured pearls are less valuable than natural pearls, whereas imitation pearls have almost no value. One way that jewelers can determine whether a pearl is cultured or natural is to have a gem lab perform an X-ray of the pearl. If the X-ray reveals a nucleus, the pearl is likely a bead nucleated saltwater pearl. If no nucleus is present, but irregular and small dark inner spots indicating a cavity are visible, combined with concentric rings of organic substance, the pearl is likely a cultured freshwater pearl. Among cultured pearls, Akoya pearls from Japan are some of the most lustrous. Although imitation pearls look the part, they do not have the same weight or smoothness as real pearls, and their luster will also dim greatly.

F Historically, the world's best pearls came from the Persian Gulf, especially around what is now Bahrain. The pearls of the Persian Gulf were naturally created and collected by breath-hold divers. Unfortunately, the natural pearl industry of the Persian Gulf ended abruptly in the early 1930s with the discovery of large deposits of oil. The water pollution resulting from spilled oil and indiscriminate overfishing of oysters essentially ruined the pristine waters of the Gulf that once produced pearls. Still, Bahrain remains one of the foremost trading centers for high quality pearls. In fact, cultured pearls are banned from the Bahrain pearl market, in an effort to preserve the location's heritage. Nowadays, the largest stock of natural pearls probably resides in India. Ironically, much of India's stock of natural pearls came originally from Bahrain. Unlike Bahrain, which has essentially lost its pearl resource, traditional pearl fishing is still practiced on a small scale in India.

G Pearls also come in many colours. The most popular colours are white, cream, and pink. Silver, black, and gold are also gaining interest. In fact, a deep lustrous black pearl is one of the rarest finds in the pearling industry, usually only being found in the South Sea near Australia. Thus, they can be one of the more costly items. Nowadays, pearls predominantly come from Japan, Australia, Indonesia, Myanmar, China, India, the Philippines, and Tahiti. Japan, however, controls roughly 80% of the world pearl market, with Australia and China coming in second and third, respectively.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 1–4

Reading Passage 1 has seven paragraphs, A–G.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

ABCDEFG
1 difficulties in the cultivation process
2 causes affecting the size of natural pearls
3 ancient customs around pearls
4 distinctions between cultured pearls and natural ones

Questions 5–10

Complete the summary using the list of words, A–K, below.

Throughout history, people in used pearls for medicine and philtres. There are essentially three types of pearls: natural, cultured and imitation. Natural and cultured pearls share a similar growing process, while imitation pearls are different. And owns the reputation for its imitation pearl industry. The country usually produces the larger pearls due to the favourable environment along the coastline, while the nation of manufactures some of the most glistening cultured pearls. In the past, the country in the Persian Gulf produced the world's best pearls. At present, the major remaining suppliers of natural pearls are in .

A America
B Philippines
C Australia
D Bahrain
E China
F Japan
G India
H Egypt
I Myanmar
J Persia
K Mallorca

Questions 11–13

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

11 A cultured pearl's centre is often significantly larger than that in a natural pearl.

12 Imitation pearls are usually the same price as natural ones.

13 Akoya pearls from Japan glow more deeply than South Sea pearls from Australia.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 珍珠素有 “珠宝皇后” 之称，其历史魅力远超如今佩戴者的认知。在有记载的大部分历史中，一串品相均匀的天然珍珠项链是价值连城的珍宝，堪称世界最昂贵珠宝。20 世纪初养殖珍珠出现前，天然珍珠稀有昂贵，仅限贵族与富豪拥有。古埃及人尤其喜爱珍珠，许多统治者将珍珠视为珍宝，常随葬珍珠藏品；在东方及波斯帝国，珍珠被研磨成昂贵粉末，用于治疗心脏病、癫痫，还可能用作催情药；中国悠久历史也充分证明珍珠的重要性。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 珍珠通常分为三类：天然珍珠、养殖珍珠和仿珍珠。天然珍珠形成于特定牡蛎、贻贝或蛤蜊体内 —— 当沙粒等异物进入，贝类为防御会分泌液体包裹异物，层层沉积后形成有光泽的珍珠。养殖珍珠形成过程相同，唯一区别是异物为人工植入的珠核或贝壳碎片（称为珠母贝），这些贝壳本身也价值不菲，是培育优质珍珠的关键 “催化剂”，其形成的珠核比天然珍珠大得多。仿珍珠则完全不同，通常是玻璃珠蘸取鱼鳞制成的溶液，涂层薄且易脱落，一般可通过咬珍珠辨别真假。西班牙马略卡岛（Mallorca）以仿珍珠产业闻名。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 无论何种珍珠，培育过程通常需数年：贻贝需 3 年达到成熟年龄，之后自然或人工植入异物；异物植入后，珍珠还需 3 年才能长至最大尺寸。期间常出现异物被排斥、珍珠畸形、贝类因病死亡等问题，5-10 年周期结束后，仅 50% 的贝类存活，产出的珍珠中仅约 5% 品质达标，可用于顶级珠宝制作。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 普通人如何判断珍珠价值？光泽与尺寸是核心考量：光泽取决于珍珠层的细腻均匀度，光泽越深、形状越完美、表面越光滑，价值越高；尺寸则与贝类年龄（成熟贝类产更大珍珠）及培育地点相关 —— 澳大利亚南海域因海底富含营养，且当地常见贻贝偏好产大珍珠，故常产出大珍珠。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 通常养殖珍珠价值低于天然珍珠，仿珍珠几乎无价值。珠宝商可通过宝石实验室 X 光鉴别珍珠类型：若 X 光显示珠核，多为海水有核养殖珍珠；若无珠核，但有不规则小暗点（表明有空腔）及有机物质同心环，则多为淡水无核养殖珍珠。日本阿古屋珍珠（Akoya）是最具光泽的养殖珍珠之一；仿珍珠虽外观相似，但重量、光滑度不及真珍珠，光泽也会大幅暗淡。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 历史上，全球最佳珍珠产自波斯湾（尤其如今的巴林周边），这些天然珍珠由自由潜水者采集。不幸的是，1930 年代初波斯湾发现大量石油，天然珍珠产业戛然而止：石油泄漏污染海水，过度捕捞牡蛎破坏了曾盛产珍珠的纯净海湾环境。如今巴林仍是优质珍珠主要交易中心，为保护遗产，巴林珍珠市场禁止销售养殖珍珠。目前全球天然珍珠最大存量可能在印度，讽刺的是，印度的天然珍珠多源自巴林；与巴林失去珍珠资源不同，印度仍小规模保留传统采珠业。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 珍珠颜色多样，最受欢迎的是白色、奶油色和粉色，银色、黑色和金色也逐渐受青睐。其中，色泽浓郁的黑珍珠是珍珠行业最稀有品种，通常仅产于澳大利亚附近南海域，价格高昂。如今珍珠主要产自日本、澳大利亚、印度尼西亚、缅甸、中国、印度、菲律宾和塔希提，日本控制全球约 80% 的珍珠市场，澳大利亚和中国分别位居第二、第三。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落匹配（Questions 1–4：Which paragraph contains the following information?）

items.text:
（1）题目 1：difficulties in the cultivation process
题目翻译：培育过程中的困难
答案：C
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “Often, the irritant may be rejected, the pearl will be terrifically misshapen, or the oyster may simply die from disease or countless other complications. By the end of a 5 to 10 year cycle, only 50% of the oysters will have survived. And of the pearls produced, only approximately 5% are of a quality substantial enough for top jewelry makers”，明确列举培育中的困难（异物排斥、珍珠畸形、贝类死亡、存活率低、优质率低），与题干对应，因此答案为 C。

（2）题目 2：causes affecting the size of natural pearls
题目翻译：影响天然珍珠尺寸的因素
答案：D
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “Size, on the other hand, has to do with the age of the oyster that created the pearl (the more mature oysters produce larger pearls) and the location in which the pearl was cultured. The South Sea waters of Australia tend to produce the larger pearls; probably because the water along the coastline is supplied with rich nutrients from the ocean floor. Also, the type of mussel being common to the area seems to possess a predilection for producing comparatively large pearls”，明确提到影响尺寸的因素（贝类年龄、培育地点、水质营养、贝类种类），与题干对应，因此答案为 D。

（3）题目 3：ancient customs around pearls
题目翻译：与珍珠相关的古代习俗
答案：A
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “The ancient Egyptians... Many Egyptian leaders... were often buried along with their cherished pearl collection. In the Orient and Persian Empire, pearls were ground into costly powders to cure anything from heart disease to epilepsy, with possible aphrodisiac uses as well”，描述古代埃及（珍珠随葬）、波斯（珍珠入药）的习俗，与题干对应，因此答案为 A。

（4）题目 4：distinctions between cultured pearls and natural ones
题目翻译：养殖珍珠与天然珍珠的区别
答案：B
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “The only difference between natural pearls and cultured pearls is that the irritant is a surgically implanted bead or piece of shell called Mother of Pearl... The resulting core is much larger than in a natural pearl”，直接对比两者区别（异物是否人工植入、珠核大小），与题干对应，因此答案为 B。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 2. 概要填空（Questions 5–10：Choose the correct letter, A–K）

items.text:
（1）题目 5：Throughout history, people in \___\___ used pearls for medicine and philtres.
题目翻译：历史上，\___\___的人们将珍珠用于制药和催情药。
答案：J（Persia，波斯）
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “In the Orient and Persian Empire, pearls were ground into costly powders to cure anything from heart disease to epilepsy, with possible aphrodisiac uses as well”，“medicine” 对应 “cure diseases”，“philtres（催情药）” 对应 “aphrodisiac uses”，明确提到波斯人将珍珠用于制药和催情，因此答案为 J。

（2）题目 6：\___\___ owns the reputation for its imitation pearl industry.
题目翻译：\___\___以仿珍珠产业闻名。
答案：K（Mallorca，马略卡岛）
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “The island of Mallorca in Spain is known for its imitation pearl industry”，“is known for” 对应 “owns the reputation for”，明确提到马略卡岛以仿珍珠产业闻名，因此答案为 K。

（3）题目 7：The country \___\___ usually produces the larger pearls due to the favourable environment along the coastline.
题目翻译：\___\___因沿岸有利环境，通常产出更大珍珠。
答案：C（Australia，澳大利亚）
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “The South Sea waters of Australia tend to produce the larger pearls; probably because the water along the coastline is supplied with rich nutrients from the ocean floor”，明确提到澳大利亚南海域产大珍珠，因此答案为 C。

（4）题目 8：The nation of \___\___ manufactures some of the most glistening cultured pearls.
题目翻译：\___\___生产部分最具光泽的养殖珍珠。
答案：F（Japan，日本）
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “Among cultured pearls, Akoya pearls from Japan are some of the most lustrous”，“lustrous” 对应 “glistening”，明确提到日本阿古屋珍珠光泽度高，因此答案为 F。

（5）题目 9：In the past, the country \___\___ in the Persian Gulf produced the world’s best pearls.
题目翻译：过去，波斯湾的_\___\__产出全球最佳珍珠。
答案：D（Bahrain，巴林）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Historically, the world’s best pearls came from the Persian Gulf, especially around what is now Bahrain”，明确提到波斯湾巴林附近产最佳珍珠，因此答案为 D。

（6）题目 10：At present, the major remaining suppliers of natural pearls are in \___\___.
题目翻译：目前，天然珍珠的主要剩余供应国是_\___\__。
答案：G（India，印度）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Nowadays, the largest stock of natural pearls probably resides in India”，“largest stock” 对应 “major remaining suppliers”，明确提到印度是天然珍珠主要存量国，因此答案为 G。

items.text:
（1）题目 11：A cultured pearl’s centre is often significantly larger than that in a natural pearl.
题目翻译：养殖珍珠的中心通常比天然珍珠大得多。
答案：TRUE（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “The resulting core is much larger than in a natural pearl”，“core” 对应 “centre”，“much larger” 对应 “significantly larger”，明确提到养殖珍珠珠核更大，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 TRUE。

（2）题目 12：Imitation pearls are usually the same price as natural ones.
题目翻译：仿珍珠价格通常与天然珍珠相同。
答案：FALSE（错误）
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “cultured pearls are less valuable than natural pearls, whereas imitation pearls have almost no value”，明确提到仿珍珠 “几乎无价值”，与天然珍珠价格差异巨大，与题干描述矛盾，因此判定为 FALSE。

（3）题目 13：Akoya pearls from Japan glow more deeply than South Sea pearls from Australia.
题目翻译：日本阿古屋珍珠的光泽比澳大利亚南海珍珠更深。
答案：NOT GIVEN（未提及）
解析：Paragraph D 提到澳大利亚南海珍珠 “尺寸大”，Paragraph E 提到日本阿古屋珍珠 “光泽度高”，但未比较两者 “光泽深度”，无相关信息，因此判定为 NOT GIVEN。
